Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact: sustained latency and 503s on reserved pool (ClearCore)

Priyom —

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency and a growing 503 error rate against our reserved capacity this morning (approx 08:00 PDT). Token throughput for our main inference route (model: open-redwood-xl-v2) is ~45% below the expected committed throughput; retries are spiking. This is impacting user-facing inference in our analytics dashboard (users seeing timeouts).

Quick details:
- First observed: 07:55 PDT
- Error rate (5xx) peaked at 12.4% between 08:05–08:20
- Average P95 latency up from ~180ms to ~1.2s
- We have attached a short metric snapshot and a log snippet.

We need immediate help: is this on your side (dedicated farm saturation / overflow) or something in our request patterns? We’re open to temporary mitigations — bursting, throttling noncritical routes, fallback to hosted, anything that buys us time while we triage.

Please advise next steps and whether you need anything from our side (more logs, call, authorization).

— Jenna Lowe
Head of Platform, ClearCore Analytics
ops@clearcore.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, Jenna Lowe <ops@clearcore.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: sustained latency and 503s on reserved pool (ClearCore)

Quick triage notes — from infra/serving: 

Observations (08:30–08:44 PDT):
- Dedicated GPU pool assigned to ClearCore shows continuous queue growth on hotpath shards; GPU utilization is at 98–100% across the pool.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% (likely due to a surge of diverse request prefixes this morning).
- One worker node entered a degraded state and restarted twice between 08:10–08:18 (logs attached to ticket).
- We’re also seeing increased sequence lengths on a small subset of requests (long-context scoring flows), which amplifies token processing time and headroom pressure.

Immediate actions taken (08:40–08:44 PDT):
- Kicked a rolling restart for the degraded worker and put it on a 5-minute health-check hold.
- Dispatched autoscale signal — but reserved pool autoscaling respects customer commit; it requires explicit burst authorization to consume additional shared capacity.
- Enabled short-term request shaping for noncritical endpoints in ClearCore’s route config (reduces concurrency for low-priority calls).

Proposed plan (explicit asks below):
1) Authorization to allow a 2-hour burst allocation on shared headroom so we can drain the queue and stabilize. If approved we will: increase concurrency cap by 30% and accept burst traffic to reduce queue depth.
2) Recommend enabling a 10% fallback to our hosted replica for noncritical traffic (reduces load on reserved pool).
3) Engineering will investigate root cause for KV-hit regression and whether a mis-sampled prefix distribution caused the cache miss event. Expect initial RCA in 24 hours.

If we get burst authorization I can push the config change within 12 minutes and monitor. Priyom — can you confirm whether ClearCore can sign off on a short burst?

— David Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: clearcore-ops-log-snippet.txt

Subject: ClearCore post-mitigation readout and exec ask: quota burst + follow-up RCA

Naomi, Marissa — quick readout and ask for executive attention. Summarized timeline below for the exec notes.

Summary:
- 08:12 — ClearCore ops reported degradation (JIRA-INFR-4821).
- 08:40 — Infra identified saturation: 98–100% GPU utilization, queue growth, degraded worker restarts.
- 08:44 — Engineering enabled request shaping and attempted rolling restart. Autoscale signal issued but gated by reserved commit.
- 09:05 — ClearCore provided signed burst authorization; we opened a 2-hour burst window and enabled 10% hosted fallback.
- 09:07 — Queue depth reduced and 5xx rate dropped from 12.4% to <1% within ~10 minutes. P95 latency returned close to baseline by 09:25.

Root-cause hypothesis: short-lived spike in long-context scoring requests combined with a temporary drop in prefix KV cache hit-rate; worker instability amplified headroom pressure. Engineering will complete a full RCA within 24 hours (JIRA-INFR-4821).

Exec asks:
1) Authorization to approve a temporary credit/one-time invoice adjustment for ClearCore’s emergency burst usage (they were within committed tier but needed short shared capacity). We should offer a goodwill concession for the first hour of burst to preserve the relationship.
2) Approve a follow-up cross-functional post-mortem with Product, Serving, and Customer Success to reduce recurrence risk (proposed date: 2027-04-28 10:00 PDT).

Customer impact: degraded dashboard experience for ~25% of users for ~45 minutes until mitigation fully took effect. No data exposure.

Next steps we own:
- David: full RCA and remediation plan + timeline (24h).
- Priyom: coordinate exec authorization on credits and schedule post-mortem.
- CS/AM: follow up with ClearCore with apology and summary of remediation.

I recommend we approve a one-hour credit and run the post-mortem on the proposed date. If you approve, I’ll draft the customer email and the credit memo.

— Priyom Das
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
